tagline: A self-hosted small-team chat with channels, threads, and search
verdictSummary: Real-time channel-based chat with threads and search is a genuine weekend-to-week build on a normal web stack — the mechanics aren't the hard part. What is: the trust of an existing team already living inside Slack, native mobile push notifications, and the moderation and abuse-handling infrastructure that matters the moment a community grows past people you know personally.
coreLoopDIY: Host a private chat space with channels and threaded replies, deliver messages in real time over WebSockets, and keep full history searchable, for a team that already trusts hosting it themselves.
whatYouLose: the network effect of a team already on Slack
native mobile apps with push notifications
enterprise moderation, SSO, and compliance tooling
whyPeopleStillPay: Chat itself is a commodity; what a team is really paying for is not having to be the one who gets paged when real-time delivery breaks for two hundred people at once, or who has to handle abuse reports personally.
prompt: Build a small, self-hosted team chat: channels, threaded replies, reactions, and search — scoped to a team you already trust, not a public community platform. Use Next.js/TypeScript with WebSockets for live delivery and Postgres as the durable store (every message is written to Postgres first; WebSocket delivery is a notification on top, not the source of truth). Support channels (public within the workspace, or invite-only), threaded replies attached to a parent message, emoji reactions, @mentions with a notification list, and file attachments stored on local disk or S3-compatible storage. Add full-text search across message history using Postgres's built-in search. Implement two roles — owner (can manage members and channels) and member — with an invite-link flow instead of open signup. Send an email digest of unread mentions for members who aren't actively online, so notifications don't depend on a native mobile app. Do not build voice or video calling, native mobile apps, or enterprise SSO/compliance features — those are out of scope; this is a web-only chat for a team small enough to invite by hand. Requires hosting, a domain, and a transactional email provider for the digest — no other external service needed.

faq.q: Can I invite people the way I would to a Slack workspace?
faq.a: Yes, via an invite link an owner generates — there's no open signup, and no directory of other workspaces to discover, since this isn't trying to be a public network.

faq.q: Will I get push notifications on my phone?
faq.a: Not as native push — the closest substitute here is the email digest for unread mentions. Real mobile push notifications need a native app this build doesn't include.

faq.q: Does it support voice or video calls?
faq.a: No, that's out of scope. Pair it with an existing scheduling link and any video-conferencing service for calls.

faq.q: What does it cost to run?
faq.a: Hosting, a domain, and a database — typically a few dollars a month for a small team, with no per-seat fee, versus Slack Pro's per-user monthly price.
